name: The balance point that stuck at 68 centimetres
subject: practical_science
brief: Ishan Sheikh is using a one-metre Wheatstone bridge in the physics room to compare a 4 ohm standard coil with a 4 ohm plug in a resistance box. The galvanometer should balance near the 50 centimetre mark, but it balances stubbornly at 68 centimetres. The store lends one spare part at a time and writes each one down.

causes.name: A loose, tarnished brass taper plug in the resistance box adds extra contact resistance
A dry, oxidised solder joint at the zero-centimetre copper strip adds hidden end resistance
The sliding jockey knife-edge is bent and reads two centimetres off the wooden scale
The centre-zero pointer on the galvanometer is mechanically stuck

tests.name: Inspect the brass plugs and the copper end strips for dull oxide and firm seating
Sight down the jockey blade against the metre rule and the end terminal
Measure the resistance box and its plugs with the bench ohmmeter
Measure the millivolt drop across the zero-end joint while current flows
Balance again with the demonstrator's spare jockey

note: Uses Ishan Sheikh (npc_ishan_sheikh) at Nabapara Vidyalaya (loc_nhss). Two equal resistances balance at the midpoint; a null at 68 cm means the left arm carries extra resistance, here a dry, oxidised joint at the zero end of the wire. The tests were rewritten so that each positive result follows from its cause: the spare jockey changes the reading only if the jockey is bent, the end-strip voltage drop is large only for a bad joint.
